significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that the measurable "knowledge axis" lies approximately in the span of belief and truth and exhibits a positive conjunctive interaction, with departures predicting factivity failures. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanistic relation, constraining expected knowledge readouts and error patterns across belief/truth combinations rather than merely showing that an epistemic direction exists; it would also clarify whether truth-oriented methods such as Marks and Tegmark's The Geometry of Truth and Li et al.'s Inference-Time Intervention capture only one component of epistemic status. True and false are distinguishable: a negative result would rule out the proposed compositional JTB geometry, although it would not identify the alternative mechanism. Topic-substitution check: generic research on LLM beliefs would not imply this conjunction law or its predicted coupling to factivity errors, so the score reflects the claim-specific increment.

reach.justification: The named handle is "a diagnostic for which of the three axes a given model has failed to separate," supplemented by the measurable conjunction interaction between belief, truth, and knowledge readouts. As worded, it is mainly post hoc because it diagnoses an existing representational collapse and correlates it with "KaBLE-style factivity accuracy," rather than explicitly forecasting unseen failures before they occur. After per-model re-extraction, however, the hypothesis predicts a transferable relation—knowledge should approximate the belief/truth conjunction—and the stated "cross-model comparison" makes this useful to model evaluators and auditors beyond the immediate mechanistic study. Topic-substitution check: the topic alone supplies neither this diagnostic nor the transferable conjunction rule, so the reach score is based on the claim-specific handle.
